baseline_derivation: On an actually established canonical graph p(q,a,v,w)=P(q), the implicit gauge rate derivative is v_a=-A^-1 C_m,a and w_a=-M^-1 C_p,a.
For H=P dot (v,w)-L, H_a=R0_a+e_L,m dot v_a+e_L,p dot w_a=R0_a-C_m,a^T lambda_m-C_p,a^T lambda_p, with A^T lambda_m=e_L,m and M^T lambda_p=e_L,p.
The correction therefore uses target-minus-literal e_L, not epsilon. Even epsilon=0 leaves e_L=-Delta unless the independently measured literal/registered bridge vanishes.

At a noncanonical current point, using these current blocks defines a specific residual extension/frozen-baseline diagnostic. It is not an exact fixed-target reduced physical normal value until the canonical graph/rate solution is earned; retain current epsilon and bounded inverse residuals.

Original239 already evaluates the fixed-rate partial -L_a, so do not add another identical fixed-rate action variation. Apply exactly one negative mixed-adjoint feedback, preserving all weak spatial rows and the separate time-primary ports.
canonical_and_direct_rate_elimination: Mechanical and phase canonical Newton rows: A delta_v+C_q,m delta_q=epsilon_m; M delta_w+C_q,p delta_q=epsilon_p. Their right-hand sides remain epsilon, never e_L.
When these inverse applications are earned, delta_v=A^-1(epsilon_m-C_q,m delta_q), delta_w=M^-1(epsilon_p-C_q,p delta_q).

The direct normal differential is delta_R0=B_q delta_q+R_v delta_v+R_w delta_w;290 supplies B_q at fixed rates,87 supplies R_v/T_v, and the new cached phase-rate contact supplies R_w. This yields B_q-R_v A^-1 C_q,m-R_w M^-1 C_q,p plus the affine R_v A^-1 epsilon_m+R_w M^-1 epsilon_p.
CMC differential similarly uses T_q delta_q+T_v delta_v; the declared phase temporal variation of this geometric CMC is zero. CMC does not receive -C_a^T lambda as an extra row term.
Do not use both an explicitly computed delta_v and a second -R_v A^-1 C_q delta_q term, or add R_v A^-1 epsilon twice. Those are alternative forms of the same eliminated rate contribution.
